title: Counit-transpose cancellation for the smooth exceptional comparison
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient datum of [def-pur-conventions]: $k$ is the fixed algebraic closure of $\mathbf F_q$ of characteristic $p$, $\ell\ne p$, and $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ with $n\geq1$. Let $X,Y,Y'$ be finite-type $k$-schemes, let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type $k$-morphism and let $v:Y'\to Y$ be an arbitrary $k$-morphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Form the Cartesian square [def-cbc-compact-support-square] with $X'=X\times_YY'$, projections $u:X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to Y'$, so $f\circ u=v\circ f'$. Choose a compactification $c=(j,p)$, $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y$ with $j$ a quasi-compact open immersion and $p$ proper [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], and let $c'=(j',p')$ be its pullback. Then $\overline X$ and $\overline X'=\overline X\times_YY'$ are finite-type $k$-schemes, so they have finite dimension and [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] applies to $c$ and $c'$.

Use the ordinary constant-$A$ module derived categories on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. For each scheme $T$ write $C_T=\nu_T^*$ for the exact derived comparison pullback [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback], $U_T=R\nu_{T,*}$, and $\eta_T:\operatorname{id}\xrightarrow{\sim}U_TC_T$ for the unit on $D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison]. For every arrow $q:T'\to T$ write $\kappa_q:C_{T'}q_{\mathrm{et}}^*\xrightarrow{\sim}Lq_{\mathrm{proet}}^*C_T$ for the canonical comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. Put $F_c^e=Rp_{\mathrm{et},*}j_!^{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support], $F_c^p=Rp_{\mathrm{proet},*}j_!^{\mathrm{proet}}$, and similarly $F_{c'}^e,F_{c'}^p$. For $N\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ let $C_{c,N}:C_YF_c^eN\xrightarrow{\sim}F_c^pC_XN$ be the canonical compact-support comparison, the inverse of the map of [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison] for the identity witness, built from the extension-by-zero and normalized proper direct-image comparisons as in [lem-pur-co-smooth-exchange-transport]; define $C_{c',N'}$ for $N'\in D^+(X'_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ in the same way. Put
$$S_N=Lv^*(C_{c,N})\circ\kappa_{v,F_c^eN},\qquad T_N=F_{c'}^p(\kappa_{u,N})\circ C_{c',u_{\mathrm{et}}^*N}.$$
Let $E^e_N:v_{\mathrm{et}}^*F_c^eN\to F_{c'}^eu_{\mathrm{et}}^*N$ be the compact-support exchange of [def-cbc-exchange-map], an isomorphism by [thm-cbc-finite-torsion], and let $E^p_{C_XN}:Lv^*F_c^pC_XN\to F_{c'}^pLu^*C_XN$ be the chosen-compactification pro-etale exchange of [lem-pur-co-smooth-exchange-transport]. By that lemma $T_N\circ C_{Y'}(E^e_N)=E^p_{C_XN}\circ S_N$, so $E^p_{C_XN}$ is an isomorphism.

Let $R=f_c^\times$ and $R'=f'^\times_{c'}$ be the ordinary etale right adjoints of $F_c^e$ and $F_{c'}^e$ [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], with counits $\varepsilon^e,\varepsilon'^e$ and Hom bijection $J'$ for $F_{c'}^e\dashv R'$. Let $G\in D^+(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ be such that $M=RG$ and $R'v_{\mathrm{et}}^*G$ are bounded below. Define
$$\varepsilon^p_G=C_Y(\varepsilon^e_G)\circ C_{c,M}^{-1}:F_c^pC_XM\to C_YG.$$

(1) As maps $C_{Y'}F_{c'}^eu_{\mathrm{et}}^*M\to C_{Y'}v_{\mathrm{et}}^*G$,
$$\kappa_{v,G}^{-1}\circ Lv^*(\varepsilon^p_G)\circ(E^p_{C_XM})^{-1}\circ T_M=C_{Y'}\bigl(v_{\mathrm{et}}^*\varepsilon^e_G\circ(E^e_M)^{-1}\bigr).$$

(2) Let $\beta^e_G:u_{\mathrm{et}}^*M\to R'v_{\mathrm{et}}^*G$ be the $J'$-transpose of $v_{\mathrm{et}}^*\varepsilon^e_G\circ(E^e_M)^{-1}$. Use for $F_{c'}^p$ and $H'=C_{X'}R'U_{Y'}$ the transported bounded-below Hom bijection of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class], normalized as in [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]: for $N'\in D^+(X'_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $L\in D^+(Y'_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ it sends $z:F_{c'}^pC_{X'}N'\to L$ to $C_{X'}\bigl(J'(U_{Y'}(z\circ C_{c',N'})\circ\eta_{Y',F_{c'}^eN'})\bigr)$, and on an input with witness $\alpha:C_{X'}N'\xrightarrow{\sim}K'$ one first precomposes with $F_{c'}^p\alpha$ and finally precomposes with $\alpha^{-1}$. Let $\beta^p_G:Lu^*C_XM\to H'Lv^*C_YG$ be the transpose, for the witness $\kappa_{u,M}$, of $Lv^*(\varepsilon^p_G)\circ(E^p_{C_XM})^{-1}$. Then
$$\beta^p_G\circ\kappa_{u,M}=C_{X'}R'\bigl(U_{Y'}(\kappa_{v,G})\circ\eta_{Y',v_{\mathrm{et}}^*G}\bigr)\circ C_{X'}(\beta^e_G),$$
that is, the pro-etale counit-transpose comparison is the conjugate of $C_{X'}(\beta^e_G)$ under the isomorphisms $\kappa_{u,M}$ and $C_{X'}R'(U_{Y'}(\kappa_{v,G})\circ\eta_{Y',v_{\mathrm{et}}^*G})$. Both identities are natural in $G$. No separatedness of $X$, $Y$ or $Y'$, no smoothness of $f$ and no invertibility of $\beta^e_G$ or $\beta^p_G$ is assumed, and no adjunction on all pro-etale objects is used.

source.place: Transport of compact-support base change and transposition: the counit substitution and cancellation identifying the two transposes.

proof.text:
Fix the compactification $c=(j,p)$ and its pullback $c'=(j',p')$ of [def-cbc-compact-support-square]; $f'$ is separated of finite type and $c'$ is a compactification of it by that definition. $A$ is a finite commutative ring and $f$ is separated of finite type, so [lem-pur-co-smooth-exchange-transport] applies to the square with $u,T,U$ there read as $f,X,Y$ here and $w,u'$ as $u,f'$. Its map $C_{c,L}$ (normalized proper direct-image comparison $b_p$ followed by $Rp_{\mathrm{proet},*}$ of the extension-by-zero comparison $e_j$) is, by the explicit formula $c_{G,\mathrm{id}}=b_{p}^{-1}\circ Rp_{\mathrm{proet},*}(e_j^{-1})$ in [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison], the inverse of that lemma's comparison for the identity witness; this is the $C_{c,N}$ of the statement, and likewise $C_{c',N'}$. Its $a_v,a_w$ are the natural isomorphisms $\kappa_v,\kappa_u$ of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback], and its $E^e_u$ is the exchange $E^e$ of [def-cbc-exchange-map]. Hence $S_N,T_N$ are exactly the lemma's $S_L,T_L$ at $L=N$, and the lemma gives, naturally in $N\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$,
$$T_N\circ C_{Y'}(E^e_N)=E^p_{C_XN}\circ S_N.$$

source.place: Transport of compact-support base change and transposition: identify the chosen compactification comparisons and the exchange.

proof.text:
By [thm-cbc-finite-torsion] (finite commutative $\Lambda=A$, $f$ separated of finite type with compactification $c$, $v$ arbitrary, $N\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$), $E^e_N$ is an isomorphism, hence so is $C_{Y'}(E^e_N)$. The factors $C_{c,N}$, $C_{c',u^*_{\mathrm{et}}N}$, $\kappa_{v,F^e_cN}$, $\kappa_{u,N}$ are isomorphisms, so $S_N$ and $T_N$ are isomorphisms. By the identity of step 1, $E^p_{C_XN}=T_N\circ C_{Y'}(E^e_N)\circ S_N^{-1}$ is a composite of isomorphisms, hence an isomorphism, and
$$(E^p_{C_XN})^{-1}\circ T_N=S_N\circ C_{Y'}(E^e_N)^{-1}=S_N\circ C_{Y'}\bigl((E^e_N)^{-1}\bigr).\qquad(*)$$

source.place: Transport of compact-support base change: invertibility of the etale exchange and transported pro-etale exchange.

proof.text: Domains. $G\in D^+(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $M=RG$ is bounded below by hypothesis, so $u^*_{\mathrm{et}}M$ is bounded below (exact inverse image) and $v^*_{\mathrm{et}}G\in D^+(Y'_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. By [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback] all $C_T$-images are bounded below, and $Lv^*C_YG$, $Lu^*C_XM$ are bounded below via $\kappa_{v,G},\kappa_{u,M}$. Hence $N'=u^*_{\mathrm{et}}M$ with witness $\kappa_{u,M}:C_{X'}N'\xrightarrow{\sim}Lu^*C_XM$ and $L=Lv^*C_YG$ lie in the domain of the class-restricted bijection of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] for $c'$ (its dimension hypothesis holds since $\overline X'$ is finite type over $k$, as recorded in the statement), and its formula, as normalized in [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] and displayed in the statement, applies. The units $\eta_{Y'}$ at $F^e_{c'}N'$ and at $v^*_{\mathrm{et}}G$ are isomorphisms natural in their argument by [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison]. The map $\varepsilon^p_G=C_Y(\varepsilon^e_G)\circ C_{c,M}^{-1}$ is the pro-etale counit by definition in the statement; no further property of it is used.

source.place: The adjunction bijections and counits transport: write the counit formula by transposing the identity.

proof.text:
Identity (1). Take $N=M$ in $(*)$ of step 2 and expand $S_M=Lv^*(C_{c,M})\circ\kappa_{v,F^e_cM}$:
$$\kappa_{v,G}^{-1}\,Lv^*(\varepsilon^p_G)\,(E^p_{C_XM})^{-1}T_M=\kappa_{v,G}^{-1}\,Lv^*\bigl(C_Y(\varepsilon^e_G)\circ C_{c,M}^{-1}\bigr)\,Lv^*(C_{c,M})\,\kappa_{v,F^e_cM}\,C_{Y'}\bigl((E^e_M)^{-1}\bigr).$$
Functoriality of $Lv^*$ cancels $C_{c,M}^{-1}$ against $C_{c,M}$, leaving $\kappa_{v,G}^{-1}\,Lv^*C_Y(\varepsilon^e_G)\,\kappa_{v,F^e_cM}$. Naturality of $\kappa_v:C_{Y'}v^*_{\mathrm{et}}\Rightarrow Lv^*C_Y$ [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] at the arrow $\varepsilon^e_G:F^e_cM\to G$ gives $Lv^*C_Y(\varepsilon^e_G)\circ\kappa_{v,F^e_cM}=\kappa_{v,G}\circ C_{Y'}(v^*_{\mathrm{et}}\varepsilon^e_G)$. Hence the left side equals $C_{Y'}(v^*_{\mathrm{et}}\varepsilon^e_G)\circ C_{Y'}((E^e_M)^{-1})=C_{Y'}\bigl(v^*_{\mathrm{et}}\varepsilon^e_G\circ(E^e_M)^{-1}\bigr)$, with source $C_{Y'}F^e_{c'}u^*_{\mathrm{et}}M$ and target $C_{Y'}v^*_{\mathrm{et}}G$. Naturality in $G$: every factor is natural in $G$ ($\varepsilon^e$, $C_{c,-}$, $\kappa$, $E^e$, $E^p$ by steps 1-2).

source.place: Transport of compact-support base change and transposition: substitute the exchange and counit formulas and cancel comparison maps.

proof.text:
Identity (2). Put $z=Lv^*(\varepsilon^p_G)\circ(E^p_{C_XM})^{-1}:F^p_{c'}Lu^*C_XM\to L$, $w=v^*_{\mathrm{et}}\varepsilon^e_G\circ(E^e_M)^{-1}$, $N'=u^*_{\mathrm{et}}M$, $\psi=U_{Y'}(\kappa_{v,G})\circ\eta_{Y',v^*_{\mathrm{et}}G}:v^*_{\mathrm{et}}G\to U_{Y'}L$. By the bijection displayed in the statement (step 3 checks its domain), with witness $\kappa_{u,M}$,
$$\beta^p_G\circ\kappa_{u,M}=C_{X'}J'\bigl(U_{Y'}(z\circ F^p_{c'}(\kappa_{u,M})\circ C_{c',N'})\circ\eta_{Y',F^e_{c'}N'}\bigr)=C_{X'}J'\bigl(U_{Y'}(z\circ T_M)\circ\eta_{Y',F^e_{c'}N'}\bigr).$$
By identity (1) of step 4, $z\circ T_M=\kappa_{v,G}\circ C_{Y'}(w)$. Naturality of $\eta_{Y'}$ [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] at $w$ gives $U_{Y'}C_{Y'}(w)\circ\eta_{Y',F^e_{c'}N'}=\eta_{Y',v^*_{\mathrm{et}}G}\circ w$, so the argument of $J'$ is $\psi\circ w$. Naturality of the Hom bijection $J'$ of $F^e_{c'}\dashv R'$ [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint] in the second variable gives $J'(\psi\circ w)=R'(\psi)\circ J'(w)=R'(\psi)\circ\beta^e_G$. Applying the functor $C_{X'}$ yields $\beta^p_G\circ\kappa_{u,M}=C_{X'}R'(\psi)\circ C_{X'}(\beta^e_G)$, which is (2); $\psi$ is an isomorphism, so this is the stated conjugation. Naturality in $G$ follows from that of every factor. Nothing used a point, a nonempty cover, smoothness of $f$ or invertibility of $\beta^e,\beta^p$, so empty schemes, zero $G$ and $v=\mathrm{id}$ are included.
